text: Anatase and rutile TiO2 powders were prepared by a sol-gel route and calcined at 450 and 800 °C, respectively. Diffuse reflectance spectra were converted with the Kubelka-Munk function, and Tauc plots gave an indirect band gap of 3.18 eV for the anatase powder and 2.98 eV for the rutile powder.

ZnO thin films were deposited on quartz by RF sputtering at 300 °C. The transmittance spectra show a sharp absorption edge located at 368 nm, from which the optical band gap of the film was estimated.

We computed the electronic structure of wurtzite GaN with VASP. The PBE functional gives a band gap of 1.65 eV, while the HSE06 hybrid functional (mixing parameter 0.25) opens the gap to 3.28 eV. The experimental value of 3.44 eV reported in the literature is thus underestimated by PBE.

Exfoliated monolayer MoS2 flakes show a strong photoluminescence peak at 1.85 eV, which we take as the direct optical band gap of the monolayer. For the bulk crystal, our PBE calculations give an indirect band gap of 1.29 eV.

ZnS nanoparticles are widely used as wide band gap phosphor hosts. Here ZnS was synthesized by a hydrothermal method at 180 °C for 12 h. XRD confirms the cubic zinc blende phase with an average crystallite size of 6 nm, and TEM shows quasi-spherical particles.

CdS films were grown by chemical bath deposition. The Urbach energy of the films is 0.15 eV, the thermal activation energy of conductivity is 0.62 eV and the work function from Kelvin probe is 4.9 eV. A Tauc analysis of the absorption spectrum gives an optical band gap of 2.42 eV.

The band gap of germanium at 300 K was determined from the temperature-dependent conductivity of an intrinsic wafer and found to be 660 meV, consistent with the thermal excitation of carriers across the fundamental gap.
An InSb photodetector cooled to 77 K showed a cut-off wavelength of 7.3 µm in its photoresponse. We attribute this cut-off to interband absorption across the band gap of the InSb absorber.

For monolayer h-BN, PBE yields a band gap of 4.6 eV. A G0W0@PBE calculation corrects it to a quasiparticle gap of 6.8 eV, and solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation gives a lowest optical gap of 6.1 eV due to a strongly bound exciton.

gold.evidence: yields a band gap of 4.6 eV

text: All-inorganic CsPbBr3 and CsPbI3 films were spin-coated and characterized by UV-vis absorption. Tauc plots give optical band gaps of 2.31 eV and 1.73 eV, respectively. For a single-junction cell the optimal gap is about 1.34 eV according to the Shockley-Queisser limit, so both films are above the ideal value.

A photocatalyst for overall water splitting must have a band gap larger than 1.23 eV. In this work, hematite Fe2O3 was found to have a band gap of 2.1 eV and monoclinic BiVO4 a band gap of 2.4 eV, both measured by diffuse reflectance spectroscopy.
Using LDA within density functional theory, the indirect band gap of bulk silicon is calculated to be 0.52 eV, which severely underestimates the experimental value of 1.17 eV reported in Ref. [12].
Photoreflectance spectroscopy on a semi-insulating GaAs wafer gives a band-edge transition at 1.519 eV at 4 K and at 1.424 eV at 300 K, consistent with the Varshni temperature dependence of the gap.

On-surface synthesized 7-AGNR on Au(111) was investigated by scanning tunneling spectroscopy. The dI/dV spectra show the valence band onset at -0.9 V and the conduction band onset at +1.0 V, yielding a transport gap of 1.9 eV for 7-AGNR on the gold substrate.
In0.53Ga0.47As lattice matched to InP shows an absorption cut-off at 1.65 µm at room temperature. The measured band gap of the InP substrate is 1.34 eV.

gold.evidence: measured band gap of the InP substrate is 1.34 eV

text: Our graph neural network predicts a band gap of 2.01 eV for Cu2O. The test-set mean absolute error of the model is 0.38 eV. The Materials Project database lists a PBE gap of 0.51 eV for the same compound, which we use as a baseline.

gold.evidence: predicts a band gap of 2.01 eV

text: SnO2 nanoparticles were calcined at 500 °C for 2 h and have an average crystallite size of 12 nm. The optical properties are studied by UV-vis spectroscopy; the absorption edge shifts to shorter wavelength with decreasing particle size, but the quantitative band gap was not extracted in this study.

Al-doped ZnO films with 0, 2 and 4 at% Al were prepared by spray pyrolysis. The optical band gap increases from 3.28 eV (undoped) to 3.35 eV (2 at% Al) and 3.41 eV (4 at% Al), which is attributed to the Burstein-Moss shift.
CdSe nanocrystals dispersed in toluene show an absorption onset at 520 nm (2.38 eV), indicating a blue shift relative to the bulk due to quantum confinement.
For NiO, the PBE+U calculation with U = 6.3 eV gives a band gap of 3.8 eV. Combined UPS and inverse photoemission spectroscopy performed on our epitaxial film measures a band gap of 4.3 eV.

gold.evidence: gives a band gap of 3.8 eV
measures a band gap of 4.3 eV

text: Sol-gel ZnO films prepared with different precursor concentrations have optical band gaps in the range 3.20-3.30 eV. For the film made from the 0.1 M solution the Tauc gap is 3.27 eV.
Ellipsometry of the amorphous Ta2O5 coating indicates a band gap above 4 eV, and we estimate it to be less than 4.5 eV from the transmission cut-off. The refractive index at 633 nm is 2.1.
After N2 plasma treatment the optical gap of ZnO nanowires narrows from 3.30 eV (untreated) to 3.12 eV (treated), a decrease of 0.18 eV.
CdS/ZnO core-shell nanorods absorb light up to 560 nm. The Tauc gap of the heterostructure is 2.52 eV, and the conduction band offset between CdS and ZnO is 0.4 eV (type-II alignment).

gold.evidence: Tauc gap of the heterostructure is 2.52 eV

text: CuInS2 nanocrystals show an absorption onset corresponding to a band gap of about 1.5 eV.
The optical band gap of TiO2 films decreases from 3.40 eV to 3.05 eV as the annealing temperature increases from 400 to 700 °C; at 550 °C it is 3.22 eV.
